questions.prompt: The soldiers were praising the gods with loud voices before the battle.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs deōs magnīs vōcibus ante proelium laudābant.

questions.prompt: The faithful farmer works in the fields while his sons sweat.
questions.answer: Agricola fidēlis in agrīs labōrat dum fīliī sūdant.

questions.prompt: The queen was calling her daughters into the great hall.
questions.answer: Rēgīna fīliās suās in magnam aulam vocābat.

questions.prompt: Tomorrow we shall free the captives whom the enemy captured.
questions.answer: Crās captīvōs quōs hostēs cēpērunt līberābimus.

questions.prompt: When you have prepared the ships, we shall sail to Greece.
questions.answer: Ubi nāvēs parāveris, ad Graeciam nāvigābimus.

questions.prompt: The general will overcome the enemy and will save the city.
questions.answer: Dux hostēs superābit et urbem servābit.

questions.prompt: You will love this poem when you have read it.
questions.answer: Hoc carmen amābis ubi id lēgeris.

questions.prompt: Having been called by the king, the messenger hurried through the gates.
questions.answer: Ā rēge vocātus, nūntius per portās festīnāvit.

questions.prompt: With the enemy conquered, the citizens celebrated a triumph with great joy.
questions.answer: Hostibus superātīs, cīvēs magnā cum laetitiā triumphum celebrāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The farmers, tired by long labor, were sweating in the hot sun.
questions.answer: Agricolae longō labōre fessī in calidō sōle sūdābant.

questions.prompt: The captured city, once free, praised its brave leaders.
questions.answer: Urbs capta, ōlim lībera, ducēs fortēs laudāvit.

questions.prompt: If you love virtue, you will avoid the corruption of the city.
questions.answer: Sī virtūtem amās, corruptiōnem urbis vītābis.

questions.prompt: Because the maiden had adorned the altar with flowers, the priest praised her.
questions.answer: Quia virgō āram flōribus ōrnāverat, sacerdōs eam laudāvit.

questions.prompt: Although the wind was blowing strongly, the sailors sailed across the sea.
questions.answer: Quamquam ventus fortiter flābat, nautae trāns mare nāvigāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The greedy merchant desired gold more than friendship.
questions.answer: Mercātor avārus aurum magis quam amīcitiam dēsīderābat.

questions.prompt: The old man told us many stories about the war.
questions.answer: Senex nōbīs multās fābulās dē bellō narrāvit.

questions.prompt: The children were showing the new house to their grandfather with joy.
questions.answer: Līberī novam domum avō cum laetitiā mōnstrābant.

questions.prompt: If the gods have preserved the fleet, we shall build a new temple.
questions.answer: Sī deī classem servāvērunt, novum templum aedificābimus.

questions.prompt: The weary soldiers are panting while they climb the steep mountain.
questions.answer: Fessī mīlitēs anhēlant dum arduum montem ascendunt.

questions.prompt: The king was governing the broad provinces with an even temper.
questions.answer: Rēx lātās prōvinciās aequā mente temperābat.

questions.prompt: The brave general overcame the enemy and freed the city.
questions.answer: Fortis dux hostēs superāvit et urbem līberāvit.

questions.prompt: By first light the merchants will have hidden their gold in the ground.
questions.answer: Prīmā lūce mercātōrēs aurum in terrā cēlāverint.

questions.prompt: The orator is telling a long tale to the assembled citizens.
questions.answer: Ōrātor cīvibus congregātīs longam fābulam nārrat.

questions.prompt: The thirsty travelers drank the cool water from the deep spring.
questions.answer: Sitientēs viātōrēs frīgidam aquam ē fonte altō pōtāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The philosopher praises virtue but condemns the greed of tyrants.
questions.answer: Philosophus virtūtem laudat sed avāritiam tyrannōrum damnat.

questions.prompt: While the stars are shining, the shepherds watch their flocks in the fields.
questions.answer: Dum sīdera lūcent, pāstōrēs gregēs suōs in agrīs spectant.

questions.prompt: The weary traveler was longing for home while he wandered through unknown lands.
questions.answer: Viātor fessus domum optābat dum per ignōtās terrās errābat.

questions.prompt: We are preparing a worthy gift for the goddess who saved the city.
questions.answer: Dōnum dignum deae parāmus quae urbem servāvit.

questions.prompt: Tomorrow the merchants will sail across the wide sea toward the islands.
questions.answer: Crās mercātōrēs trāns lātum mare ad īnsulās nāvigābunt.

questions.prompt: When you have freed the captives, the whole town will praise your name.
questions.answer: Cum captīvōs līberāveris, tōtum oppidum nōmen tuum laudābit.

questions.prompt: The general will overcome the enemy's cavalry and will guard the camp.
questions.answer: Dux equitātum hostium superābit et castra servābit.

questions.prompt: By first light the farmers will have plowed the wide fields near the river.
questions.answer: Prīmā lūce agricolae lātōs agrōs prope flūmen arāverint.

questions.prompt: The poet had celebrated the deeds of brave men in a long song.
questions.answer: Poēta rēs fortium virōrum longō carmine celebrāverat.

questions.prompt: After the storm had devastated the coast, the people implored the gods.
questions.answer: Postquam tempestās ōram vastāverat, populus deōs implōrāvit.

questions.prompt: The messengers announced that the king had freed the hostages.
questions.answer: Nūntiī rēgem obsidēs līberāvisse nūntiāvērunt.

questions.prompt: You loved wisdom when you were a boy, and now as an old man you love it.
questions.answer: Amāvistī sapientiam cum puer erās, et eam nunc senex amās.

questions.prompt: Let us praise the immortal gods and adorn their altars with flowers.
questions.answer: Deōs immortālēs laudēmus et ārās eōrum flōribus ōrnēmus.

questions.prompt: The mother is watching the road so that she may greet her returning son.
questions.answer: Māter viam spectat ut fīlium redeuntem salūtet.

questions.prompt: Love your country, young men, and always defend liberty!
questions.answer: Amāte patriam, iuvenēs, et lībertātem semper dēfendite!

questions.prompt: If the citizens loved peace, they would not prepare cruel wars.
questions.answer: Sī cīvēs pācem amārent, bella crūdēlia nōn parārent.

questions.prompt: About to fight, the general strengthened his men with a long speech.
questions.answer: Pugnātūrus dux mīlitēs suōs longā ōrātiōne firmāvit.

questions.prompt: By working hard the farmer secures a peaceful life.
questions.answer: Strēnuē labōrandō agricola vītam quiētam parat.

questions.prompt: The girl, loving music, was singing a sweet song beneath the stars.
questions.answer: Puella mūsicam amāns dulce carmen sub sīderibus cantābat.

questions.prompt: The envoys came to greet the victorious king.
questions.answer: Lēgātī rēgem victōrem salūtātum vēnērunt.

questions.prompt: Although the enemy were devastating the fields, the citizens did not despair.
questions.answer: Quamquam hostēs agrōs vastābant, cīvēs nōn dēspērāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The wise old man used to tell the boys tales worthy of memory.
questions.answer: Sapiēns senex puerīs fābulās memoriā dignās nārrābat.

questions.prompt: When the trumpet had given the signal, the horsemen seized the bridge.
questions.answer: Cum tuba signum dedisset, equitēs pontem occupāvērunt.

questions.prompt: We hope that the gods will preserve our fleet from the storm.
questions.answer: Spērāmus deōs classem nostram ā tempestāte servātūrōs esse.
